notes.text: Eventually always b — FG b, again. The second b-edge out of "last was b" is a guess, exactly like the one the Büchi automaton for this language cannot do without: it commits to "no more a's ever" and dies if an a arrives. Here it is pure decoration. Delete it and the machine still recognises FG b, because the two-state part already does.

That is the point: NcoBA = DcoBA. Nondeterminism adds nothing to what a co-Büchi automaton can recognise — every one of them can be determinised. Büchi is the odd condition out, where the guess is the difference between recognising FG b and not being able to. Compare the DcoBA example, which is this machine minus the guess.

meta.title: Eventually always b, with a needless guess
meta.blurb: FG b as a nondeterministic co-Büchi automaton, carrying a guess it does not need — a demonstration that NcoBA = DcoBA.
